The committee
A small organisation acquires too much power.

We began as a committee for the broken gate. Nobody had expected us to last beyond Thursday. By the third meeting we had a treasurer (unnecessary, since we had no money) and by the fourth, someone had suggested identification cards. The gate remained broken. I mention this because when the police arrived they seemed very interested in the cards and almost entirely uninterested in the gate, which was what I had called them about. Apparently Mr Finch had been using his to stop traffic on the high street. He said it was legitimate committee business. I said it was a laminated piece of cereal box. The treasurer objected to that description. She had paid for the laminating herself.
One condition
Someone agrees to a strange bargain.

I said he could have my dreams on weekdays. I work weekdays; I don't use them. We shook hands and he went away. That night I slept extremely well. Unfortunately he had understood 'dreams' in the ambitious sense and I woke with no interest in getting promoted, finishing my degree or learning Italian. I went to the shop and bought cheese. It was an excellent Tuesday.
apology, attempt 2
Write an apology that reveals more than intended.

Dear Helen, I am sorry about the incident at your birthday. I did not know the man was your husband. I had imagined you would introduce him at some point, but obviously you were busy. That sounded pointed. I am also sorry about the plate although I maintain it was an unsuitable surface for a candle. I will replace both. The plate and candle. Not your husband.
at the door
Write a scene in which courtesy prevents something urgent.

The woman insisted I come in. I needed a ladder; my son was stuck in her tree. She asked if I'd had lunch. I invented a sandwich because a handful of peanuts wouldn't count. She asked whether I took sugar. I said I needed a ladder, loudly, and she looked hurt. There was a walking frame by the fridge. She put both hands on the counter to turn and I understood she couldn't fetch me anything. She had been trying to make me stay long enough to fetch it myself. I asked where the cups were. Outside my son called that he could see the motorway.
Platform change
Two travellers realise they were sent to the wrong place.

'This isn't our train.'
'It's got our number.'
'Look outside.'

No platform. No tracks either. A field going backwards under us, cows standing with their heads up.

'Get the guard.'
'You get him.'

The boy at the other table was filming. His mother slapped the phone down.

'How long?' I asked her.

She looked at the window.

'Since Derby.'
Friday money
A conversation about a debt.

'You said Friday.' 'It is Friday.' 'It's nearly midnight.' He starts looking through his pockets. I tell him stop doing that, I know he hasn't got it. He asks if I want his phone. I don't want his phone. The thing has a crack across the face and it's all his daughter has to call him on. 'How much have you got?' 'Nine.' 'Nine pounds?' 'Yes.' I owe sixty to someone who won't take nine. I sit on the step. He sits beside me. Neither of us says anything for a while. Then he asks if I want a cigarette and I say yes even though I quit.
the wrong holiday
Two people remember the same event differently.

I remember the sea being green. My brother says it was a reservoir and we weren't allowed in. But there was a man selling rubber rings. Why would he sell them there? He says I'm combining two holidays. Probably am. Dad bought a yellow ring and it deflated before we reached the car. Unless that was the holiday with Joan. There are three photographs of the same wall and none of the thing I want to remember.
please destroy after reading
A young person leaves instructions for their future self.

Dear future me. If we are still living here when you find this you need to leave. I dont care what mum says about the deposit. Also don't marry Craig, even if he gets his motorbike back. I know that sounds random but you will know why. I have hidden twenty pounds behind the radiator for you. It might have fallen down by now so use a ruler. Please dont turn into somebody who finds this funny. I am serious. I am going to be serious for the rest of my life actually. Starting tomorrow because it's Lydia's tonight and she has got the karaoke from her uncle.
homework
Remember something you got wrong at school.

I wrote that whales were fish and cried when it got marked wrong because my dad told me. I thought the teacher was calling him stupid. I didn't say that, I just cried which made the other kids laugh. Wish I had said it now. Not to win, just so she knew why I was making such a fuss over a whale.
Runaway assembly
A repair goes wrong while the machine is moving.

Left actuator sticks. I kick the casing and get six more steps out of it. Enough to clear the loading bay. Behind me the doors start closing and if they shut I'm trapped in this thing until morning with a battery fire under the seat. Pull the release. Nothing. Pull harder. Handle comes away in my hand. Great. The suit keeps walking, one long step one short, straight at a stack of fuel drums. I kill the right leg. We turn instead of stopping. Should have expected that. There is a gap between the drums and the wall just wide enough for me if I can get the left shoulder round. Metal shrieks. The visor fills with a red warning I can't clear because the touch panel is cracked and now something hot has reached the back of my knee.
Bench notes
Write about a machine that behaves differently each time you test it.

Motor runs with the cover off.
Cover on, stops.
Wire pinched? no.
Spindle clearance? fine.
Magnet in the cover? no.

 Spent two hours on it and then Mel said try holding the cover nearby. Starts slowing down before it even touches. Move it away, speeds up. I took the lid to the other end of the shop and the motor accelerated until the belt came off. It is a piece of aluminium. I am looking at a piece of aluminium that the motor doesn't like. I have measured it. I have weighed it. I don't know what else you can do to a lid.
spare
A replacement part almost fits.

Wrong thread. Knew it as soon as I turned it but kept going. Now it's cross threaded and stuck and I have converted one broken thing into two. Nice work. Need the hacksaw. No I need to stop touching it for five minutes.
Manual override
Two people must repair a dangerous system together.

Pressure gauge stuck on zero. Can't be zero, the pipe is shaking. Vic tells the kid to shut the valve. Wheel turns but the shaft doesn't. Stripped coupling. He reaches for pliers and the pipe jumps, knocks his mug off the bench. Hot water everywhere. He says leave it. The kid reaches for the mug. No, leave the BUILDING. Vic shoves him through the door. Outside people are coming down the road to see what the noise is. He waves them back.
might be a shortcut
A person follows directions they do not understand.

He said follow the music. There was music in three directions so I picked loudest. Ended up at a wedding. They gave me a plate before I could explain and I was hungry so I stopped explaining. A girl asked who I was and I said a friend. She told an auntie. The auntie asked which friend. I pointed generally at the door but the groom was there. She shouted for him. I still had a spoon in my hand when he came over. Told him I was looking for the bus station.
just walking
Write a freewrite about something you do when you are restless.

sometimes I walk till my feet hurt so I can blame being in a bad mood on that. which is backwards I know. yesterday went past the mosque and the car wash and all the way to the big roundabout. there was a shoe on the central bit. one little glittery girls shoe. How. anyway I kept going, shouldn't have becuase the road stops having pavement and then you're just a person next to lorries. had to climb a fence to get off it. tore my trousers not even in a cool place right on the back. Got home and mum said you've been out ages did you get milk. I had specifically gone out for milk. So went back out. actually that part was fine.
THE ELECTION
An animal wins an election and has to govern.

the mayor is a horse. I dont mean he looks like one hes an actual horse. people voted for him as a joke and now there are hay deliveries blocking the town hall. first meeting he ate the budget so technicly we are solvent? I dont know what solvent means exactly but we have no budget now. the deputy is a man who understands horses but doesnt understand bins. the bins havent been collected for six weeks no five weeks. People keep saying at least hes honest and then he bites a child. now there is a debate about whether the child provoked him. I am moving. I have been saying I am moving since the previous mayor who was a normal man and much worse at least the horse doesnt own the car park.
geese plan
List the steps of an unlikely escape.

ONE steal a goose
TWO teach goose to carry rope
THREE realise goose already knows how, become suspicious
FOUR follow goose to other prison
FIVE discover second goose waiting with tiny bolt cutters

I haven't worked out six. I want them to be in love but they both look the same to me and I keep mixing up which one has the rope. One has a scar now. That helps.
An apology to the moon
An enormous creature tries to do something delicate.

Sorry about the tides I was putting it back. Hard to judge distance through somebody else's spectacles. Forgot I had them on. The moon is closer now but only on Tuesdays. Fill out a form if your boat is in a tree. Don't climb the tree. It may also move. I'm doing my best with six hands and none are my dominant hand because I haven't decided which that is. The little people keep running about while I work. One has made a flag. I can't read it without the spectacles and we've seen how that goes.
A small discrepancy
A person notices their workplace owes them money.

Fourteen pounds short. Again. I took four payslips to Ruth. She said payroll was complicated. I said multiplication wasn't. Wished I hadn't because she gives me Saturdays off. She asked me to leave it with her. I wanted the papers back. I had written bus fares on the back to show why fifty six pounds mattered. She turned one over and read them. I felt stupid. Shouldn't have to explain why I want money I've worked for. But I explained and she kept nodding and nothing got agreed.
inventory
A tenant moves out and records everything.

two keys, one works if you lift the door first
Meter 047193
Marks on kitchen wall already there, have photos
Table belongs to upstairs, told him twice
Carpet wet BEFORE we moved in

 I sound angry reading this back but I need it written down. He keeps saying we all make mistakes as if that covers six months of a leaking ceiling. The man who came to view it had a baby in a carrier. I wanted to tell him about the ceiling. Landlord stood between us the whole time and talked about natural light. There is natural light through the hole now so I suppose that bit was true.
the extra chair
An unexpected expense changes a plan.

We can afford four chairs. There are five of us. I say I'll stand and everyone says don't be silly but nobody says which chair they will give up. The woman in the shop is waiting. I ask if the display one is cheaper. It isn't.
compulsory fun
Write an opinion you have difficulty saying aloud.

I don't think work has to be a family. I have a family and some of them are difficult enough without adding the man who checks my timesheet. We had to write one personal goal on a board today and mine was get home on time. The facilitator said think bigger. I said get home on time every day. She left it there but put a star by someone else's goal to run a marathon. Good for him. I would like to see my children while they are awake. That seems quite a big thing to me. I didn't say that last part in the room, of course. I wrote it here instead and I am still annoyed about the star.
The water budget
A space crew discovers a hidden passenger.

The tank was down eleven litres. I assumed a leak until I found a child's sock in the laundry intake. There were no children on the manifest. I showed it to Hale. She sat down very slowly and asked me to close the hatch. Her son was asleep behind the insulation in her cabin, thin enough to fit where an adult couldn't. She had been sharing her ration with him for nineteen days. We were beyond the return burn. I told her we had to tell the captain. She said yes, then asked for one hour. Not to escape, there was nowhere to go. She wanted to wash him first. I gave her my water card and went to the bridge without her.
Aphelion
Describe an ordinary task in an unfamiliar environment.

The potatoes have roots but no idea which way to grow. We turn the trays every morning. Today a root caught the velcro on my sleeve and I dragged the whole plant out. Little white net of roots hanging between me and the tray. Leon helped free it with nail scissors. We put it back in the blue light. Tomorrow I'll try a cage from the mesh over the fans. Might be worse. I don't know enough about potatoes. None of us do. Should have brought a gardener.
The fence
Two neighbours try to fix something together.

We put the first post in backwards. You wouldnt think a post could be backwards but there is a bit for the next bit to fit in and ours was facing the wrong garden. Steve said leave it and we can turn the next one round. That didnt sound right but he is good at this stuff usually. We did four before his wife came out and said where is the gate going. We had forgot the gate. All the panels were laid out in a row and there wasnt any space for it. Steve got quite cross then, not with her but with the measurments. He said somebody had moved the string. It was me I had moved it to get wheelbarrow through. I said maybe we should have some tea.
Captain
Someone is given responsibility unexpectedly.

They made me captain because I was oldest. Bad reason really. I couldn't remember the names yet. Two lads called Dan so I said tall Dan and small Dan and small Dan didnt like that. Now I have to choose who isnt playing and I dont want to. Thought you just wore the band and did the coin bit.
first lap
Do something for the first time in years.

I ran to the end of the road and had to stop. In my head I was still good at running. My actual body had other ideas. A woman with a buggy went past me, running, and then an old bloke walking quite fast. I walked behind him for a bit pretending that was the plan. At the corner I did another little run. It wasnt much. Got home all sweaty and my son said did you go to the shops. No. Just the corner really. I'll go again Thursday.
inside the hem
A repair reveals evidence someone needs.

Coins in the hem. Cora felt them knocking her knuckles as she lifted the skirt. She cut two stitches. A silver disc fell out, stamped with a face from the news. Not a coin. The girl on the chair stopped swinging her feet. Where had the dress come from? Her mother had said bring it here and wait. A car stopped outside, engine running. Cora put the disc in her mouth before she could think why. It tasted of soap. She told the girl to get under the cutting table.
wings
Someone makes a costume that works too well.

She used fencing wire for the bones and old silk for the skin. When she lifted the wings they lifted her. Only an inch at first; her heels came out of her shoes. She laughed and pulled harder. The workroom shrank below her, pins glinting on the table, the iron still plugged in. There was no room to turn. Her left wing caught the light fitting and the wire bent. Now one side was higher than the other. She reached for a shelf and missed, scattering boxes of thread. The window was open but not wide enough. She would have to fold one wing, and the moment she did that she began to fall sideways towards the glass.
lining test
Describe a material without naming it.

Warm where it's been against skin. Slippery the other way. Little catches under my nail, almost invisible until I pull. Smells of someone else's perfume and the cupboard. I keep writing soft but that's wrong. It's thin. Thin isn't the same.
fitting room 2
A person finally says what they want.

The zipper wouldnt go up. She said sorry to the girl helping her, sorry to her sister, almost sorry to the dress itself. Her sister said breathe in. She was already breathing in. She had been breathing in since she left the house. A pin scratched the soft part under her arm and suddenly she was angry. Not beautifully angry. Hot and red and a bit wet around the eyes. She said take it off. The girl said there was another size and she said no take it OFF. Her sister went quiet. Once she was back in her own t shirt she could think again. She wanted the blue suit she'd seen downstairs. She had wanted it all morning but everyone kept bringing dresses.
